# Metric cards and the MCDA pipeline

A metric card declares fields for identity, kind, inputs, output, semantics, comparability, implementations, examples, and provenance. See [measurement theory](measurement-theory.md) and [normalization and scales](normalization-and-scales.md) for the scale types and the normalization strategies.

## Fields read

- `polarity`: `normalize` inverts `lower_is_better` columns and rescales each column to [0, 1], higher is better.
- `range_lower`, `range_upper`: when both are declared, [`run_from_registry`](../reference/run_from_registry.qmd) passes them to `normalize`, and min-max and baseline-relative use them instead of the observed extrema. A value outside the declared range raises.
- `comparability.recommended_normalization`: the strategy for the column, by default `min_max`. The options are `min_max`, `log_min_max`, `rank`, `zscore`, `baseline_relative` and `target_relative`.
- `semantics.score_of_random_baseline`: the chance-level value, used by `baseline_relative`.
- `semantics.target`: the ideal value, used by `target_relative`.
- `scale_type`: `validate_for_aggregation` refuses `nominal` and `ordinal` columns for every aggregation.
- `allowed_transformations`: `validate_for_aggregation` checks that the card allows the transform of the strategy. Min-max, baseline-relative and target-relative need `affine` or `min_max`; `log_min_max` needs `log`; `rank` needs `rank`; `zscore` needs `z_score` or `affine`.
- `comparability.recommended_aggregation_across_datasets`: `aggregate_across_datasets` uses it to reduce a tool by dataset matrix to one value per tool. Runtime and peak memory declare `geometric_mean` (Smith 1988, [10.1145/63039.63043](https://doi.org/10.1145/63039.63043)); bounded metrics declare `arithmetic_mean`.

For a min-max column `run_from_registry` warns when a declared bound is missing or the column is heavy-tailed. The warnings are in the `Result` and the run continues.

## Fields declared but not enforced

- `meaningful_zero` and `monotonic`: no reader.
- `uncertainty_model`: uncertainty is not propagated through aggregation.
- `comparability.comparable_within` and `aggregation_rules`: notes for readers.
